cards.en: seeming to be everywhere
cards.example: Smartphones are ubiquitous in large cities.
cards.translation: Los móviles son omnipresentes en las grandes ciudades.
cards.prompt: Smartphones are ___ in large cities.

cards.en: strange because it does not fit its surroundings
cards.example: The modern sign looked incongruous on the old building.
cards.translation: El cartel moderno desentonaba en el edificio antiguo.
cards.prompt: The modern sign looked ___ on the old building.

cards.en: to place different things next to each other to show a contrast
cards.example: The film juxtaposes luxury with poverty.
cards.translation: La película yuxtapone el lujo y la pobreza.
cards.prompt: The film ___s luxury with poverty.

cards.en: done quickly with little interest or care
cards.example: He gave the report a perfunctory glance.
cards.translation: Echó un vistazo superficial al informe.
cards.prompt: He gave the report a ___ glance.

cards.en: having more than one possible meaning and not expressing a clear opinion
cards.example: Her answer was equivocal, so we asked again.
cards.translation: Su respuesta fue ambigua, así que volvimos a preguntar.
cards.prompt: Her answer was ___, so we asked again.

cards.en: to make something less clear or harder to understand
cards.example: The extra jargon only obfuscates the main point.
cards.translation: La jerga adicional solo dificulta entender la idea principal.
cards.prompt: The extra jargon only ___s the main point.

cards.es: eufórico; muy feliz por una buena noticia o un logro
cards.en: extremely happy and excited because something good has happened
cards.example: After winning the scholarship, she felt elated and celebrated with her family.
cards.translation: Tras conseguir la beca, se sintió eufórica y lo celebró con su familia.
cards.prompt: After winning the scholarship, she felt ___ and celebrated with her family.

cards.es: desilusionado al descubrir que algo no era como esperabas
cards.en: disappointed after discovering the truth about someone or something you admired
cards.example: She became disillusioned with the organisation after discovering its empty promises.
cards.translation: Se desilusionó con la organización al descubrir que sus promesas eran vacías.
cards.prompt: She became ___ with the organisation after discovering its empty promises.

cards.es: resentimiento; enfado que persiste por una situación no deseada o injusta
cards.en: anger about something you have been forced to accept
cards.example: Being forced to work unpaid overtime caused resentment among the staff.
cards.translation: Tener que hacer horas extra sin cobrar provocó resentimiento entre el personal.
cards.prompt: Being forced to work unpaid overtime caused ___ among the staff.

cards.es: remordimiento; pesar por algo malo que has hecho
cards.en: sadness and regret about something you have done
cards.example: He felt remorse for lying to his friend and apologised sincerely.
cards.translation: Sintió remordimiento por haber mentido a su amigo y se disculpó sinceramente.
cards.prompt: He felt ___ for lying to his friend and apologised sincerely.

cards.es: nostalgia; alegría y algo de tristeza al recordar el pasado
cards.en: pleasure mixed with slight sadness when remembering the past
cards.example: The old family photos filled her with nostalgia for her childhood.
cards.translation: Las antiguas fotos familiares la llenaron de nostalgia por su infancia.
cards.prompt: The old family photos filled her with ___ for her childhood.

cards.es: consternación; disgusto o decepción ante algo inesperado
cards.en: unhappiness and disappointment at an unwelcome event
cards.example: To his dismay, he discovered that the exam had been brought forward by a month.
cards.translation: Para su consternación, descubrió que el examen se había adelantado un mes.
cards.prompt: To his ___, he discovered that the exam had been brought forward by a month.

cards.en: to publicly support or suggest an idea, development or way of doing something
cards.example: Many doctors advocate a daily walk for people who sit all day.
cards.translation: Muchos médicos recomiendan un paseo diario a quienes pasan el día sentados.
cards.prompt: Many doctors ___ a daily walk for people who sit all day.

cards.en: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true
cards.example: After hours of debate, she had to concede that he was right.
cards.translation: Tras horas de debate, tuvo que admitir que él tenía razón.
cards.prompt: After hours of debate, she had to ___ that he was right.

cards.en: to make someone less confident, less powerful or less likely to succeed
cards.example: Constant criticism can undermine a child's confidence.
cards.translation: Las críticas constantes pueden socavar la confianza de un niño.
cards.prompt: Constant criticism can ___ a child's confidence.

cards.en: to make a public statement of your approval or support for something or someone
cards.example: The mayor will endorse the new bus plan at the meeting.
cards.translation: La alcaldesa respaldará el nuevo plan de autobuses en la reunión.
cards.prompt: The mayor will ___ the new bus plan at the meeting.

cards.es: poner en duda; discutir que algo sea cierto
cards.en: to disagree with something that someone says
cards.example: Few people would dispute that exercise is good for health.
cards.translation: Poca gente pondría en duda que el ejercicio es bueno para la salud.
cards.prompt: Few people would ___ that exercise is good for health.

cards.en: to take legal action against a person or organization, usually to claim money for harm they caused
cards.example: She decided to sue the company for the damage to her house.
cards.translation: Decidió demandar a la empresa por los daños a su casa.
cards.prompt: She decided to ___ the company for the damage to her house.

cards.en: the decision made at the end of a trial after judging the facts
cards.example: The jury took three days to reach a verdict.
cards.translation: El jurado tardó tres días en llegar a un veredicto.
cards.prompt: The jury took three days to reach a ___.

cards.en: the legal right or duty to care for a child after its parents have separated
cards.example: After the divorce, the mother was given custody of the children.
cards.translation: Tras el divorcio, la madre obtuvo la custodia de los niños.
cards.prompt: After the divorce, the mother was given ___ of the children.

cards.en: to officially accuse someone of a crime in a law court
cards.example: The state decided to prosecute him for fraud.
cards.translation: El estado decidió procesarlo por fraude.
cards.prompt: The state decided to ___ him for fraud.

cards.en: allowed by law, or reasonable and acceptable
cards.example: He had a legitimate reason to complain.
cards.translation: Tenía un motivo legítimo para quejarse.
cards.prompt: He had a ___ reason to complain.

cards.en: the fact of not giving enough care or attention to someone or something
cards.example: The accident was caused by the driver's negligence.
cards.translation: El accidente fue causado por la negligencia del conductor.
cards.prompt: The accident was caused by the driver's ___.

cards.en: to communicate an idea or feeling without saying it directly
cards.example: She didn't say it directly, but she implied that the plan had failed.
cards.translation: No lo dijo directamente, pero dio a entender que el plan había fracasado.
cards.prompt: She didn't say it directly, but she ___ that the plan had failed.

cards.en: to form an opinion or guess that something is true because of the information that you have
cards.example: From his tone, I inferred that he was unhappy with the decision.
cards.translation: Por su tono, deduje que no estaba contento con la decisión.
cards.prompt: From his tone, I ___ that he was unhappy with the decision.

cards.en: not loud, bright, noticeable, or obvious in any way
cards.example: There is a subtle difference between the two colors.
cards.translation: Hay una diferencia sutil entre los dos colores.
cards.prompt: There is a ___ difference between the two colors.

cards.en: to say that someone has done something illegal or wrong without giving proof
cards.example: The journalist was criticized for alleging that the minister had lied, without offering any proof.
cards.translation: Criticaron al periodista por alegar que el ministro había mentido sin ofrecer ninguna prueba.
cards.prompt: The journalist was criticized for ___ that the minister had lied, without offering any proof.

cards.en: having or expressing more than one possible meaning, sometimes intentionally
cards.example: His answer was so ambiguous that nobody knew what he meant.
cards.translation: Su respuesta era tan ambigua que nadie sabía qué quería decir.
cards.prompt: His answer was so ___ that nobody knew what he meant.

cards.en: to form an understanding that is not correct of something that is said or done
cards.example: I misinterpreted her silence as anger, but she was just tired.
cards.translation: Interpreté mal su silencio como enfado, pero solo estaba cansada.
cards.prompt: I ___ her silence as anger, but she was just tired.
